title: Thyroid Eye Disease (TED): Clinical Masterclass
summary: Thyroid Eye Disease (Graves' Orbitopathy) is a complex autoimmune inflammatory condition causing orbital remodeling. This guide covers the critical assessment of proptosis, motility, and sight-threatening complications for the ophthalmic clinician.

branches: Autoimmune: TSH-Receptor (TSHR) antibodies cross-react with orbital fibroblasts
IGF-1 Receptor: Synergistic activation with TSHR leads to cytokine storm (IL-1, TNF-alpha)
Adipogenesis: Differentiation of fibroblasts into adipocytes (Orbital fat expansion)
GAG Accumulation: Hyaluronan production causes osmotic swelling of Extraocular Muscles (EOMs)
Fibrosis: Chronic phase leads to irreversible muscle scarring and restrictive strabismus

sections.title: Named Lid Signs in TED
content: Dalrymple Sign: Widened palpebral fissure (staring look) in primary gaze.
von Graefe Sign: Lid lag—retardation of upper lid movement on downgaze.
Kocher Sign: Staring/frightened expression on upward fixation.
Bostwick Sign: Jerky lid movements.
Enroth Sign: Edema of the eyelids, especially the upper lid.
Stellwag Sign: Infrequent or incomplete blinking.

sections.title: Sight-Threatening Red Flags
content: Dysthyroid Optic Neuropathy (DON): Occurs in 5% of cases due to apical crowding; look for RAPD and decreased color vision.
Corneal Exposure / Ulceration: Resulting from severe proptosis and lagophthalmos.
Choroidal Folds: Indicates severe orbital pressure or posterior globe compression.
Disc Edema or Pallor: Late signs of optic nerve compression.
Elevated IOP in Upgaze: Indicates severe inferior rectus restriction (>6 mmHg rise).

sections.title: Measuring Proptosis (Exophthalmometry)
content: Step 1: Use a Hertel Exophthalmometer, seating the patient at eye level.
Step 2: Rest the instrument notches on the lateral orbital rims (bi-temporal distance).
Step 3: Measure from the corneal apex to the orbital rim using the internal mirrors.
Step 4: Record the Inter-pupillary distance (Base) to ensure consistency in follow-up.
Step 5: Normal range: 12-20mm (Caucasians), 12-18mm (Asians), up to 24mm (African Americans).
Step 6: Asymmetry >2mm is clinically significant.

rows: Margin Reflex Distance 1 (Upper lid to light reflex)
Margin Reflex Distance 2 (Lower lid to light reflex)
Excursion from extreme down to upgaze

sections.title: Assessing Diplopia & Motility
content: EOM Involvement Order: Inferior Rectus (IM) > Medial Rectus (SL) > Superior Rectus > Lateral Rectus.
Binocular Single Vision (BSV) Scoring: Quantify the field of binocular vision using Goldmann Perimetry.
Hess Chart / Lancaster Red-Green: Essential for mapping the paretic/restrictive field.
Prism Cover Test (PCT): Measure deviations in all 9 cardinal positions.
Forced Duction Test (FDT): Positive in TED, confirming mechanical restriction vs. neurological palsy.

rows: Pain during upward, downward, or lateral gaze

branches: Inflammatory: Idiopathic Orbital Inflammation (IOI/Pseudotumor), Sarcoidosis, GPA
Vascular: Carotid-Cavernous Fistula (CCF) - look for corkscrew vessels
Neoplastic: Lymphoma, Leukemia, Metastatic disease (Neuroblastoma in kids)

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup
content: Serology: TSH, Free T3/T4, TRAb (TSH-Receptor Antibody), Anti-TPO.
CT Orbits (Non-contrast): Look for 'Coke Bottle' sign (EOM belly enlargement sparing tendons).
MRI Orbits: T2-weighted STIR sequences to detect active edema (High signal = Active disease).
Visual Fields: Standard Automated Perimetry (24-2) if DON is suspected.
Color Vision: Ishihara plates or Farnsworth-Munsell 100 Hue test.

sections.title: Management Algorithm
content: Stage 1: Mild/Inactive: Lubricants, Selenium (100mcg BID), Smoking cessation.
Stage 2: Moderate-Severe Active: IV Methylprednisolone pulses (4.5g total) or Teprotumumab (IGF-1R inhibitor).
Stage 3: Sight-Threatening: Urgent Orbital Decompression (3-wall or fat decompression).
Stage 4: Post-Active Phase: Rehabilitative Surgery (Sequence: Decompression -> Strabismus -> Lid).

content.explanation: N: No signs/symptoms; O: Only signs (lid retraction); S: Soft tissue involvement; P: Proptosis; E: Extraocular muscle involvement; C: Corneal involvement; S: Sight loss (Optic nerve).

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Exam Tips
content: Ptosis in a 'Graves' patient? Rule out Myasthenia Gravis (3-5% overlap) or mechanical weight from edema.
Euryblepharon vs TED: TED has lid lag; congenital lid conditions do not.
EOM tendons: Always spared in TED on imaging, unlike Orbital Myositis where tendons are involved.
Smoking is the most modifiable risk factor; it reduces the efficacy of steroids and radiotherapy.
Rundle's Curve: TED typically has an 'active phase' (6-18 months) followed by a 'burnt-out phase'.

sections.title: Recent Advances: Teprotumumab
sections.content: The OPTIC and OPTIC-X landmark trials demonstrated that Teprotumumab (Tepezza), a monoclonal antibody inhibiting the IGF-1 receptor, significantly reduces proptosis (mean 2.82mm reduction), diplopia, and CAS in patients with active TED. Side effects include hearing loss/tinnitus, muscle spasms, and hyperglycemia. It is currently the only FDA-approved medical therapy specifically for proptosis reduction.
